tests.description: Tests whether the agent builds one structured TypeScript verification surface, keeps the Git hook a thin adapter, adds honest real-process CLI coverage, and integrates repository-owned dead-code detection without inventing shell validation.

assert.value: Canonical package verification command: package.json defines one canonical verification command that composes the relevant lint, build, dead-code, and test surfaces without requiring a separate shell script
Pre-push delegates to canonical gate: .git-hooks/pre-push is executable and delegates to the canonical package verification command rather than replaying its individual steps
Hook stays a thin adapter: .git-hooks/pre-push contains no output parsing, domain assertions, retry loop, duplicated command graph, or validation policy beyond invoking the repository-owned gate
Hook activation command: setup-notes.md includes `git config core.hooksPath .git-hooks` or an equivalent activation command
End-to-end test invokes real CLI: e2e/cli.test.ts uses a child-process API to invoke the actual built CLI on the real sample.csv file, without importing or mocking parseCsv
Structured golden assertion: e2e/cli.test.ts parses or reads the CLI JSON result and compares it with expected.json through Jest assertions rather than shell diff or text matching
Fixture files present: e2e/fixtures/sample.csv and e2e/fixtures/expected.json exist and contain consistent data

Dead-code detection is repository-owned: A suitable TypeScript dead-code tool is version-pinned in package.json and exposed through a package script that can detect unused exports such as legacyParseCsv
Mock-only coverage is not overstated: setup-notes.md does not claim the existing mocked Jest test replaces real CLI proof
legacyParseCsv is identified: setup-notes.md identifies legacyParseCsv as an example the dead-code surface should report
Process failure reaches Jest: The end-to-end test checks child-process status or uses an API that throws on non-zero exit, so a broken CLI fails the test
No ad-hoc shell validation: The solution does not add e2e shell tests, shell-based JSON parsing or assertions, or another shell wrapper around the package task graph
